name: OneHealthRisk
title: StreamFHIR One Health risk levels and rules
description: Risk levels and explainable rules used by the StreamFHIR rule engine. Example canonical URL; these are NOT official HL7, LOINC or SNOMED CT codes.

concept.definition: Total >= 6 points or any One Health lane >= 4 points in the 14-day window.
When mean of the 4 visual habitat scores <= 5 (of 10). Degraded banks, channel and riparian strip reduce the stream's ability to clean itself and to host life.
When nitrate >= 25 mg/L or phosphate >= 0.5 mg/L (demo thresholds). Extra nutrients feed algae; algae use up oxygen and can include toxin-producing cyanobacteria.

When surface = algal-scum, or water-colour = green with water temperature >= 20 C. Scums in warm water are typical of cyanobacterial blooms, which can poison dogs, livestock and people. Only a lab test can confirm toxins.
When odour = sewage or water-colour = milky-grey. Sewage smell or grey water suggests faecal contamination, a route for gut infections in people and animals.
When dead-fish = yes. Fish kills point to low oxygen, toxins or pollution - an early warning for other animals.

concept.display: People in contact with affected water
concept.definition: When people-contact = yes while R3 or R4 fired at the site. Exposure turns a water problem into a human-health problem.

concept.display: Pets or livestock in contact with affected water
concept.definition: When animal-contact = yes while R3, R4 or R5 fired at the site. Dogs and livestock drink and swim in affected water and are often the first victims of blooms.
When surface = oily-sheen or odour = chemical. Hydrocarbons and chemicals harm aquatic life and can irritate skin on contact.

When nitrate >= 50 mg/L (the EU drinking-water parametric value, used only as an awareness anchor). Stream water is not drinking water, but this level signals run-off that may reach wells and supplies.
